summary: Yoshifumi Honjo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1975) under Hajime Sakurabe. His career includes posts at Kyoto University, Kobe Women's University, Bukkyo University, Otani University, and Anshin-in.

Yoshihide Yoshizu (1943–2014) worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his doctorate at Komazawa University, where he also served as a lecturer (attested 1973–1996) and later as a professor (attested 2014).

Yoshihiko Nasu specializes in Buddhist studies. He held posts as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007), at Social Welfare Corporation Kongojushinkai, and as psychological director at Kongoju (attested 2017).

Yoshihiko Sakurai specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2001) and later held posts there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2003) and as a researcher at Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Senta (attested 2003).
Yoshitoyo Ohara (born 1968) works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held appointments at Kyoto University (attested 2006) and Kyoto National Museum (attested 2016).

Yoshihito Muroji is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg (1992) under Lambert Schmithausen and held posts at Kyoto University, Koyasan University (attested 1995–2012), and Shiga University of Medical Science (attested 2014–2015).

Yoshiko Shimabukuro (born 1911) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed studies at Kyoto Chuo Bukkyo Gakuen through 1936 and at Kyoto Women's University from 1936 to 1940.

Yoshinobu Kimoto (born 1950) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He held appointments as an assistant professor at Yonezawa Women's Junior College (attested 1989) and at Koshien Junior College.

Yoshinori Takeuchi (1913–2002) specialized in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1933 to 1936 and served as a professor there from ~1959 to 1976.

Yoshio Kawakatsu (1922–1984) worked in Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1945–1948) and under Paul Demiéville (~1958–1961), and he held an academic post at Kyoto University from ~1952 to 1984.

Yoshiro Imaeda (born 1947) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Ariane Macdonald and Bernard Frank, later serving as a researcher at the CNRS (~1974–2012).

Yoshiro Tamura (1921–1989) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1946–1949). He held professorial posts at Toyo University, the University of Tokyo, Rissho University, and the University of Chicago.

Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) was a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He held posts at Nagoya University (~1957–1968), Kyoto University (attested 1967–1969), Kyoto Sangyo University (~1974–1981), and Hanazono University (~1981–1986).

Yoshitsugu Sawai (born 1951) works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard universities, supervised by John B. Carman. From ~1985, he served as professor and dean of human studies at Tenri University.

Yoshiyasu Yonezawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held appointments at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 1998–2006) and as a specially appointed full-time lecturer (attested 2015).
Yoshiyuki Kawazoe (born 1947) studied at Tohoku University from ~1966 to 1975. He subsequently held an academic post at Tohoku University from ~1975 to 2012.
Yosho Nomura (1916–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University (~1936–1939) and later served there as a professor (~1963–1987) and director (~1981–1987).

Youru Wang works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean, later holding posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and Rowan University.

Yozo Taniyama (born 1972) specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1991–1996) and held positions at St. Thomas University, Japan (~2005–2008), Shitennoji University (~2008–2012), Tohoku University (~2012), and Sophia University (~2014).
Yu Yan Pang specializes in Buddhist studies. Pang earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, where doctoral supervisors were Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, and studied under Eric Kvan.
